producer_report.summary:
Added `check_reading_coverage` (new module `crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs`). It is wired as one `step!` line in `refusing_check`, after `check_scope_limit`. It refuses a reading that leaves out a bullet under the request's `Acceptance:` heading and names the bullet, its best score and the 25% threshold. The refusal text says to cover the bullet in the bullet's own words or ask the split as a question; a split may be proposed only as a question, never by dropping a bullet.

**Scoring (answers the earlier soundness finding).**
- Each bullet is scored by the share of its own content stems found in its best-matching criterion.
- No word is removed because the request's prose repeats it.
- Word forms agree (flagged/flags/flag, queued/queue, ordering/order).
- `test`, `show` and `pass` are dropped as generic stems. They are also dropped from criteria, because they pad every test-related score.
- A criterion that holds a word only a sibling bullet has, none that only this bullet has, and matches the sibling better is that sibling's and does not count for this bullet.
- A steward bullet "The change is made as described: <title>" is not scored.
- A request allows a split only when its own prose has an affirmative modal or imperative naming the job, request or work, with no negation and no question mark. "Do not split this job" and code prose like "Split the output into two columns" allow nothing.
- Readings that ask a question or decline, and requests with no Acceptance heading, are not checked.

**Measured on the real records.** `records/` was in the evidence snapshot, so the fixtures are the recorded text:
- Over the 793 accepted readings in the snapshot, 8 are newly refused (1%), and none of the newest 50.
- The omitted sza7 status bullet scores 22%. The lowest covered bullet across sza7, ttnw and bp5e is 42%. ttnw's lowest is 60% and bp5e's is 50%.
- I read two of the eight refusals in full (199q, 1fva). Each really leaves out a bullet of its request. I did not read the other six.
- The 25% threshold sits 3 points above the omitted sza7 bullet. Threshold and stem lists were tuned on a replay of those readings, so the 793-reading figure is in-sample.
- That replay was a temporary test, removed afterwards. The measured figure is therefore not reproducible from the diff; the verifier can reproduce a per-job result with `athena check-reading`.

**Wiring and tests.**
- `reading.rs` gets `mod coverage`, `pub use coverage::*` and `coverage.rs` in the test-only `reading_source()`.
- `refusal_corpus.rs` gets ten input-form tags (52 → 62), 15 `coverage-*` cases (8 refused, 7 accepted), the test `coverage_replay_over_the_corpus_and_recorded_shapes` and the test `reading_coverage_refusal_is_declared_intended`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` gets one Unreleased Added entry.
- `drain.rs`: `queue_steward_request` now adds one bullet, "the tests still pass", which the scripted readings in that file repeat. Without it 12 drain tests were refused for the steward's stock bullets.
- `fake.rs` was not needed, and I reverted my edit to it. athena-core, athena-agent and the other athena-cli tests passed without it. The cli drain tests use `common/mod.rs`'s scripted reader, not the deterministic fake.

**Departures from the plan.**
- Continuation lines join a wrapped bullet only if they start lowercase or are indented. The plan's rule also joined a "Depends on <id>" line under the last bullet and wrongly dropped that bullet's score.
- The `test`/`show`/`pass` stem filter and the steward pointer-bullet skip are additions the plan did not have. Without them the bp5e-class bullet "The root cause is named in the change description…" fell below the threshold in the replay.

open_issues: Wording in the brief: criterion 1 calls the omitted sza7 bullet 'the duration bullet'. In the recorded job it is the status-report bullet (part 3). The test names that bullet.

The 25% threshold sits only 3 points above the omitted sza7 bullet (22%). A bullet dropped from a request whose framing words are shared with other criteria could score higher and pass. The check is a floor, not proof of coverage.

The measured 8-of-793 figure came from a temporary replay test over the evidence snapshot that is not in the diff, so the verifier can only reproduce it per job with `athena check-reading`. The CHANGELOG states the figure; the verification replay measures the real rate over its own window. Threshold and stem lists were tuned on those same readings, so the 793-reading figure is in-sample.

Two kinds of bullets can be refused although a reader might think them covered: long compound bullets (e.g. 'The proof of section 5 holds: …') and boilerplate like 'No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass'. The replay refused 3 of the 8 for the long compound shape (nm2t, hvyb, n33v); I read none of them. An accepted reading that repeats the boilerplate bullet passes.
A sibling-claim edge: one criterion that merges two bullets' words (state and duration) is claimed by the first bullet, so the second is refused. A test pins this as a known limit.
mistakes: My first draft of the scorer had the stop list too short and refused the bp5e-class bullets; I found it only by replaying all 793 readings, then added the generic stems and the pointer-bullet skip.
I first wrote a fake.rs change that the suite did not need; the cli failures came from the drain.rs request helper. Reverted.
I first drafted the CHANGELOG claim that ttnw and bp5e score 42% or more, which was the sza7 figure. Fixed to the measured 60% and 50%.
learnings: records/ was present in the evidence snapshot (jobs/<month>/<job>/request.json and reading-N.json), although absent from the working copy. `Records::load_dir(evidence_dir)` and `replay_cases` let a unit test replay every accepted reading.
The cli drain tests do not use `FakeAgentDriver::deterministic()`; they use the scripted reader in crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs, with `default_reading` and `rated_scenario` readings.

`steward::from_change` adds three stock bullets ('The change is made as described: <title>', 'No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass', 'fmt, clippy and test pass') when a request has no bullets of its own, so a reading must repeat them or the request must carry its own.
Bash here refuses `tail`, `grep`, heredocs, `cd` and env-var prefixes, and the cargo wrapper holds one build slot, so a second cargo command waits up to 300 s while a long test run holds it.
Intra-doc links to private items already warn in `cargo doc --document-private-items` in this repo; that is not a lint Athena runs.
desires: A reproducible way to replay the newest accepted readings against a candidate build from a unit test, without editing a test file with a hard-coded evidence path.
Being able to read the saved tool-result files for long outputs.
